tool.title: Per-harness setup position and health
tool.description: For every harness in the checkout, run bootstrap's setup check without performing anything or touching the network, and write one `folio-harness-state/v1` file: each step in its state, the first step not done (its position) with what to do next, and health badges that are the harness's own (setup steps; the instance's committed health report, unknown without one). A recommendation is said, never acted on.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Where `<harness>.json` and `index.json` go. The deploy passes `./_site/assets/harnesses`. Absent: print the states and write nothing.

inputs.name: json
inputs.description: Print the states as JSON and write nothing.

outputs.name: states
outputs.description: One `<harness>.json` per harness and an `index.json` listing them with their positions.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: One line per harness: its position, the next step, and its badges.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: With --json, or with no --out, every harness's state as one `HarnessStates` record, in name order. Programs read this; people read `report`.

selection.when: A page or an agent needs to know, per harness, how far its setup got and what to do next, or whether the harness itself is healthy, as against its repository.
selection.limits: Offline and dry-run: a step that needs the network (documents at their IRIs, Pages live) is could-not-determine, never done. In an index that mounts an instance in part, every step looking for a file in it is could-not-determine. Built at deploy and never committed, so it describes the tree the deploy published.
selection.cost: About 6 seconds for 11 harnesses. Nothing to install, no network.

$comment.comment:
── Where each harness got to in its initialization, and how healthy it is ──

Bean `supn`, boxes 1 and 2. Owner, 2026-10-24 (card A, "Work out at publish
time"): the deploy runs bootstrap's read-only setup check on every harness
and publishes one state file each, so nothing is committed and nothing goes
stale. The steps are bootstrap-tools' `initSteps`, the tool half of
`complete-initialization.bpmn`, so this Tool satisfies bootstrap's
`initialization-steps` skill rather than keeping a second list of steps.
